ENTRY REQUIREMENTS FOR FOREIGN TOURISTS FOR IMMIGRATION INSPECTION AT INTERNATIONAL ENTRY POINTS
### ENTRY REQUIREMENTS FOR FOREIGN TOURISTS FOR IMMIGRATION INSPECTION AT INTERNATIONAL ENTRY POINTS

  1. Possess a valid passport or travel document to enter Malaysia.

  2. Possess a valid visa (for nationals of countries that require a visa to enter Malaysia).

  3. Able to explain their personal background and purpose of visit, and fully cooperate by producing relevant supporting documents throughout the immigration screening process.
  4. Not listed in the Immigration Department’s Suspect List and the Stolen and Lost Travel Documents (SLTD) database.

  5. Not classified as an prohibited or undesirable migrant.

  6. Not a Social Visit Pass (PLS) holder attempting to re-enter the country immediately due to the imminent expiration of their previous pass (commonly referred to as a “u-turn”).

  7. Possess proof of accommodation booking or confirmed lodging arrangements for the duration of the stay in Malaysia.
  8. Possess a valid return ticket to their home country or an onward ticket to a next destination country.

## Short Term Social Visit Pass

The Short term social visit pass is given to foreign visitors upon arrival for the following purposes:
  1. Social visit
  2. Visiting relatives
  3. Tourism
  4. Journalism / Reporting
  5. Meeting / Conference
  6. Business Discussion
  7. Factory Inspection
  8. Auditing Company Accounts
  9. Signing Agreement
  10. Carrying out a survey on investment opportunities/setting up factory
  11. Attending Seminars
  12. Students on goodwill missions or taking examinations at a university
  13. Taking part in sports competitions
  14. Other activities approved by the Director General of Immigration.
###### Extension of Social Visit Pass

An Extension may be given on Special consideration e.g. due to illness, accident, war in home country etc. The visitor must furnish evidence, and also present a confirmed return ticket to their home country or third country.
###### Required Documents

  1. Applicants must appear in person together with passport
  2. Form IMM.55 L295:   3. Supporting documents (if relevant)
  4. Confirmed ticket to home country or in possession of a visa and ticket to a third country

# MALAYSIA RELAXES COVID-19 TESTING RULES & TRAVEL INSURANCE FOR INBOUND TRAVELLERS

Image L64: 
PUTRAJAYA, 28 APRIL 2022 – Starting 1 May 2022, fully-vaccinated inbound travellers are no longer required to undergo pre-departure and on-arrival COVID-19 tests, including children aged 12 and below as well as for those who have been infected with COVID-19 within six to 60 days before departure to Malaysia. Travel insurance will also not be a prerequisite for foreigners entering the country.
However, inbound travellers who are not fully vaccinated against COVID-19 still need to undergo an RT-PCR test two days before departure as well as a professionally-administered RTK-Ag test within 24 hours upon arrival in Malaysia and observe a five-day quarantine (quarantine exemption is only for those aged 17 and below).
The wearing of masks outdoors is optional but still mandatory indoors, including in shopping malls, offices, public transportation and e-hailing rides. Nevertheless, face coverings are still encouraged in crowded places, and people at higher risk from COVID-19. No more physical distancing is required, and people are now free to shake hands, but they are advised to practise good hand hygiene.
Meanwhile, check-ins via the contact tracing app MySejahtera will no longer be required, but the MySJ Trace function should be activated for contact tracing. Regardless of the vaccination status, people will be allowed to enter the premises except for those who test positive for COVID-19 and have been issued a home surveillance order.
“The seven-day mandatory quarantine for positive cases remains, and the MySejahtera app is used for the COVID-19 test results submission and health assessment. However, those who test positive for COVID-19 may be released earlier from quarantine if their professionally-administered RTK-Ag test on Day 4 is negative.
For more information on the latest standard operating procedures (SOP) for travelling to Malaysia, please visit our website at https://www.malaysia.travel/travel-alert†www.malaysia.travel or Mysafe Travel portal at https://mysafetravel.gov.my/†mysafetravel.gov.my L71:

About Tourism Malaysia
Malaysia Tourism Promotion Board, also known as Tourism Malaysia, is an agency under the Ministry of Tourism, Arts & Culture Malaysia. It focuses on the specific task of promoting Malaysia as a preferred tourism destination. Since its inception, it has emerged as a major player in the international tourism scene. Prior to the pandemic, Malaysia registered 26.1 million tourist arrivals and RM86.14 billion tourist receipts, placing it among the major tourism destinations of the world.

1. Visitors must meet the following requirements before entering Malaysia:
1.1.Have a Valid Passport or Document.
a. Everyone must have a recognized and valid passport or international travel document to enter Malaysia.
b. Any passport or travel document that is not recognized by the Malaysian Government, must have a
Document replacing a Passport.
c. A passport that can be applied for at any Malaysian Representative Office abroad.
d. Holders of travel documents such as Declaration of Identity, Laiiser Passer, Titre de Voyage or Permanent
Resident Certificate of a country need to ensure that their return to their country or the country that issued
the document is guaranteed.
e. Documents must be valid for six months or more from the date of entry into Malaysia.
1.2.Have a Visa.
a. A visa is a type of endorsement in a passport or any other recognized foreign travel document that indicates
that the holder has been granted permission to enter Malaysia.
b. Foreign nationals who require a visa must first apply at any Malaysian Representative Office abroad.
c. The visa issued is not an absolute guarantee that the individual will be allowed to enter the country.
d. The final decision is at the discretion of the Immigration Officer on duty at the gate.
1.3.Have a valid return ticket and sufficient expenses.
a. Every visitor is also required to prove the financial ability to declare himself in Malaysia along with a fixed
return ticket to return to his home country or to another country.
1.4.Not an illegal immigrant.a. Any person recognized under Section 8 of the Immigration Act 1959/1963 is not allowed to enter Malaysia
despite having a valid Passport or travel document, visa, travel ticket and sufficient expenses.
1.5.Filling in the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC).
a. Visitors are required to complete a Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) / (IM.26) upon arrival at any gate of
entry gazetted at the URL https://imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main.
b. Visitors must present their passports together with a complete MDAC to the Immigration Officer on duty and
visitors must also ensure that their passports or travel documents are validated with the appropriate pass
before leaving the immigration counter.
2. About the Pass
2.1.Apart from applications to enter Malaysia for the purpose of a social or business visit, all applications for other
types of passes must be applied for before entering the country.
2.2.Each application must have a sponsor who will be responsible for the presence of the subject in the country or
for the delivery of the subject if necessary.
3. Pass Requirements.
3.1.Foreign nationals who wish to visit Malaysia must obtain a Passport at the entrance in addition to a visa (if
necessary) that allows them to stay temporarily in the country.
3.2.A passport is a type of endorsement in a passport that gives permission to stay in Malaysia for an authorized
period.

Consulate General of Malaysia, Hong Kong Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Malaysia
VISA REQUIREMENT INFORMATION
CITIZEN | TYPE OF DOCUMENT | VISA FREE PERIOD FOR VISIT NOT EXCEEDING
HONG KONG | PASSPORT | 90 days
HONG KONG | BRITISH NATIONAL (OVERSEAS) | 30 days
HONG KONG | CERTIFICATE OF IDENTITY (C.I) or DOCUMENT OF IDENTITY (D.I) | VISA IS REQUIRED
IMPORTANT NOTES:
Passport MUST remain valid for more than 6 months from the entry date into Malaysia.
The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) must be completed no later than THREE (3) DAYS BEFORE the scheduled arrival in Malaysia.
Hong Kong and Macao passport holders are required to select “Hong Kong” or “Macao” as their nationality during MDAC registration to ensure the correct visa-free period is granted. Both are now eligible to use the autogates at the available Malaysian airports.
Travellers are required to present both valid passport and a completed MDAC to Immigration officers for validation.
This information is updated as of 1 June 2026. There may be subsequent changes.

American citizens do not require a visa to visit Malaysia for business or social reasons if their stay in Malaysia is 90 days or less.
All foreign travelers are required to complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) within three (3) days prior to arrival. The MDAC is not a visa; it is a facilitation measure to expedite entry procedures.
A. Required Documents
Completed and signed Visa Application Form (IM.47)
B. Fees
USD 3.00 – United States of America Passport
